title: Adaptive shim for OpenAI Responses parity — mapping playbook and test harness
creator: Anika Patel
description: Deliver an adaptive translation shim that maps Redwood Responses API behavior to the OpenAI Responses API surface with a playbook, a test harness, and a staged rollout plan. The shim must handle: streaming chunk semantics, function/tool-calling wire format, structured output enforcement, and metadata/diagnostic passthrough. It should be resilient (graceful fallbacks), observable (parity metrics), and toggleable per-customer or per-route.
acceptance_criteria: Translation shim implemented as a runtime gateway component that can be enabled per-route
Streaming behavior: clients expecting OpenAI chunk shapes receive identical event order and field names for 95% of recorded prompts in the parity corpus
Tool/function call mapping: Redwood function-call events map to OpenAI-style call/request/complete lifecycle and back-translate results into Redwood structured outputs
Structured outputs: validators applied post-translation with configurable strictness; schema violations surfaced with clear error codes and sample input included
Automated test harness with 500+ corpus items that asserts token-level diffs, event ordering, and error-code parity
Canary rollout plan with 5% traffic, rollback conditions defined, telemetry dashboards live (parity_failures, translation_latency, error_rate)
Documentation/playbook published for SDK teams and external customers describing differences that cannot be perfectly mapped and recommended mitigations
notes: 2026-02-20: Initial scoping — collected top 100 parity failure candidates from runtime logs and support tickets. Decided to pursue an adaptive shim approach rather than changing core runtime to minimize risk to Dedicated/Private customers.

2026-02-24: Design sync with SDK leads (notes/drive: https://drive.redwood/team/responses/interop/shim-design-2026-02-24). Key trade-offs: gateway shim keeps runtime untouched but adds translation latency; in-runtime shim reduces latency but increases blast radius.

2026-03-02: Prototype demoed — maps streaming 'delta' events to OpenAI 'chunk' shape and emits 'response.create' and 'response.done' equivalents. Identified edge-case: OpenAI allows multiple tool invocations mid-stream; our runtime prefers single final tool output. Decision: support multi-invoke emulation via buffered intermediate tool events + explicit 'assistant.finish_tool' event emitted to clients.

2026-03-05: Security review kickoff — shim must not leak internal model selection headers. Added requirement to strip sensitive runtime headers and to honor KMS/HSM downstream policies. Security ticket created: SEC-342.

2026-03-08: Test harness requirements finalized. Corpus assembled (internal + anonymized customer prompts). Tests to include: event-order invariants, JSON schema equivalence for structured outputs, function-call lifecycle, token-count invariants, and mismatch classification (format, content, truncation).

2026-03-11: Integration branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4862 (shim gateway + harness). Early CI tests show 3.8% of corpus failing due to structured output schema differences (mostly required-field vs optional-field mismatches). Action: implement pre-translation coercion rules and a clear fallback that returns an OpenAI-style partial_response with 'finish_reason' = 'incomplete_schema'.

2026-03-13: Canary plan approved by SRE and Product. Metrics and dashboards created: https://observability.redwood/dashboards/responses/shim-parity. Rollout will proceed to 5% in hosted, no Dedicated or Private customers without explicit enable flag.

2026-03-14: Started writing docs for SDK teams describing the negotiation handshake (client_capabilities header) and the expected error codes. Need to finalize the telemetry event names and wire them into the Console release notes. Blocking: finalize function-call name-mapping table — see pending item in Links.

- How to represent partial streaming deltas that OpenAI folds into a single 'content' chunk? We currently emit identically shaped chunks but sometimes must merge KV cache deltas — may cause higher latency.
- What is acceptable semantic divergence with respect to function call disambiguation? (we can emulate but cannot perfectly replicate model-internal 'intent-to-call' artifacts)
- Do enterprise Dedicated customers want opt-in for shim (likely yes) or forced parity (increasing risk)? We'll survey during rollout.
